absent: Internal helper behavior for single-symbol value lookup, symbol name and value extraction, and module memory region enumeration.
Duplicate modprobe request tracking, usermode helper setup and execution semantics, security hook policy and module request tracepoint payload.
General module finder matching rules, reference counting primitives, taint flag values and panic mask handling beyond the shown mask test.
Livepatch load info layout, core symbol table construction timing, and module reference behavior during thread exit beyond put plus exit.
Sysctl registration lifetime, proc handlers, and locking for debugger module listing.

findings.text: Lookup of a named symbol value inside one module, protected by an RCU scope and delegating to an internal helper.
Iteration over defined module symbols across all modules or one named module, invoking a caller callback with name and value until the callback reports nonzero.
Debugger command that lists loaded modules with names, per-region sizes and bases, load state and, when unload is configured, use counts and dependents.
Reference count query that derives the live use count from an internal atomic counter by removing a fixed base offset.
Symbol iteration acquires the global module mutex for the whole list walk and symbol loop, releasing it on completion or early callback termination.
Single-symbol value lookup and per-CPU address probing run inside an RCU guard while traversing the global module list.
Modules in the unformed state are skipped during symbol iteration, debugger listing, exported-symbol search and per-CPU address scans.
Symbol iteration ignores undefined symbols and, when a module name filter is given, stops after the first matching module.
Symbol search context carries a half-open range of exported symbol entries plus parallel checksum and flag tables.
Global module address tree is cache aligned and starts with its minimum bound set to the all-ones address.
Module bounds tracking expands global minima and maxima from each non-empty module memory region, with a separate data range on some builds.
Maximum concurrent modprobe helper executions is fifty.
Timeout for waiting on a busy modprobe throttle is five seconds.
Module reference count base offset is one, so zero in the raw counter means going away.
Kernel request for loading a named module, formatting the name from caller arguments and either waiting for completion or only for execution start.
Module requests fail when no helper path is configured, when the formatted name would overflow its fixed buffer, when a security hook denies it, and when the concurrency throttle times out.
A synchronous module request issued from asynchronous context triggers a one-time warning because completion may deadlock against async synchronization during module init.

Helper invocation uses the configured path with a quiet flag, a separator and the module name, under a minimal environment and a killable wait mode, and announces duplicate-request outcomes in all paths.
The helper argument vector owns a duplicated module name in its fourth slot, released together with the vector by a dedicated cleanup callback.
Livepatch support copies a module ELF image into separately allocated header, section header and string table storage, and releases those three allocations on teardown.
ELF copying records the symbol section index and repoints that section address at the persistent core symbol copy because init memory is freed later; allocation failures unwind earlier allocations.
Module sysctl table exposes a string control for the helper path and an integer control for disabling modules, both with read-write owner and read-only other permissions.
The disable-modules control only permits transition from its default to the disabled value, using a min-max handler pinned at one.
Early init registers the module sysctl table under the kernel directory.
Acquisition helper rejects unformed modules as a bug, reports busy for modules still coming up, then maps reference acquisition success to zero and failure to missing.

Taint helper records the flag in the given module and globally; global tainting may disable lock debugging once when marked unreliable and may force an immediate panic when the mask intersects a panic mask.
Module name comparison treats dash and underscore as equal while comparing up to a length limit or string end.
Thread exit helper drops a module reference and then terminates the calling kernel thread with the given status without returning.
Allocated-section lookup scans from index one, requires the alloc flag and exact name match, and returns zero when absent.
Unfiltered section lookup matches by name alone from index one and returns zero when absent.
Unique-section helper counts all name matches and returns the index for exactly one, zero for none, and the negated count for duplicates.
Section address and object helpers resolve through section lookup, treating index zero as an empty section with zero address and size and deriving object counts by division.
Version lookup has two build variants: one always yields null, the other indexes a base table when present and yields null when the base is absent.
Exported-symbol search first probes the built-in table and then each formed module table, using binary search by name and enforcing license gating for restricted symbols.
Symbol name and namespace accessors handle two relocation layouts, with absent namespace represented as null in one layout.
Module lookup by name forwards to a more general finder with the full name length and exact matching.

Modules move among unformed, coming, live and going states; listings and searches hide unformed entries, acquisition refuses coming entries, and debugger output labels going, coming and live distinctly.
Module info attribute generator defines a read-only attribute with setup, show, existence test and free operations backed by a duplicated string field.
Import namespace attribute is a read-only sysfs entry whose existence depends on a stored namespace string and whose show emits that string plus newline.
Last-unloaded-module record retains fixed-size name and taint flag buffers.
Per-CPU allocation locates a fixed per-CPU section, clamps excessive alignment to a page with a warning, allocates reserved per-CPU storage and records its size; empty sections do nothing.
Per-CPU image copy replicates the initial image into every possible CPU instance.
Per-CPU address test scans formed modules with per-CPU storage under RCU and reports whether an address falls in any CPU instance, optionally canonicalizing the hit to the boot CPU instance.
Single-CPU build disables per-CPU addressing: accessor yields null, lookup always reports false, allocation only accepts an empty section, free and copy are no-ops with a size assertion.
Unload initialization seeds the reference counter at its base, initializes source and target dependency lists, and holds one extra reference during initialization.
Dependency tracking records a use edge in both the user target list and the used source list after acquiring the target; duplicate or null targets need no new edge.
Unload cleanup holds the global module mutex while walking the departing module target list, dropping each target reference and unlinking and freeing each edge.
Force-unload handling has two build variants: one treats a truncation flag as a force request and taints the kernel as unreliable, the other never forces.
Version magic inclusion and trace point creation are enabled by preprocessor definitions in the module core.
A global mutex serializes module list and state changes across symbol iteration, search validation and dependency cleanup.
Helper path storage is a fixed-length character array initialized from the configured default path.
